title: How To Avoid A Climate Disaster

questions.q: What emissions target does Gates set for the world?
a: Net zero by 2050
Net zero by 2100
Half emissions by 2030
Zero by 2060
questions.why: The overview states his clear goal is reaching zero emissions by the year 2050.

questions.q: Which activity accounts for the largest share of global emissions, according to Gates?
a: Making things such as plastic and steel
Generating electricity for homes and industry
Growing food and raising livestock
Moving people and goods from place to place
questions.why: The overview puts making things at 31 percent, ahead of electricity at 27, food at 19 and transport at 16.

A tax charged on companies that pollute
A subsidy paid to renewable energy firms
A label showing a product's energy rating
questions.why: Lesson two defines it as the added price of switching to a cleaner alternative, such as low-carbon concrete.

questions.q: How does Gates answer critics who fear nuclear power?
a: It causes fewer deaths than fossil fuels do
It has never had a serious accident
It produces no radioactive waste at all
It is cheaper to build than solar farms
questions.why: Lesson one notes that despite disasters like Chernobyl and Fukushima, nuclear's death rate is far below fossil fuels.

questions.q: What policy does Gates recommend for air conditioning?
a: Minimum energy-efficiency standards set by governments
A complete ban on new air conditioners
Higher taxes on electricity in hot regions
Free units for low-income households
questions.why: Lesson three says efficiency standards would stop people buying cheap, wasteful units and lower energy demand.
